title: Diagnostic: mutating Method on a let
hints: A `let` struct value can't change at all — not even through methods.
Change `var c` to `let c` and keep the `increment()` call.
jsBridge: A `let` struct is fully frozen, so calling a `mutating` method on it is a compile error. JS `const` only freezes the binding, and `obj.increment()` works fine. This is value semantics enforced by the compiler.

compass.q: `const c = new Counter(); c.increment()` works in JS. Why must Swift reject the struct version? What would break if it didn't?
The same code with `class Counter`: does it compile? Why?
Can you call a `mutating` method on a struct stored in a `let` array element? A `let` dictionary value?
In SwiftUI, `body` sees `self` as immutable. Is that the same rule, and why does `@State` get around it?
